messages:
eli: quick heads-up — ran a cross-region microbench for Llama/Mistral/Qwen at 8k/16k/32k and saw reproducible latency spikes for Mistral-1 (quant4a) in eu-west on H100 images. looks like an attention-phase interaction, not straight hw saturation. attaching quick notes.
samir: can you paste the exact command and kernel config you used? trying to repro locally
eli: sure — ran the standard ctx-sweep script against the serving image: 
```
./ctx-sweep --model mistral-1-8k --quant config/quant4a.json --kernels auto --seqs 8192,16384,32768 --region eu-west --instance h100-x2
```
latency jump appears >50% at ~20k seqs and higher p99 moves to double. throughput drops more than expected.
jia: did you force GQA or leave rope fallback? Qwen loves GQA, mistral sometimes falls back to rope shim depending on kernel availability
eli: left kernels=auto so fallback allowed. suspicion: our rope->gqa compatibility layer has a phase-alignment shim that behaves differently when quantized kernels pick different block sizes. looks like phase drift causes more KV cache evictions => higher latency.
marta: interesting — on Mistral we observed repetition and mild quality regressions after quant4a at long context previously. could be related. do you have samples for model outputs (top-k text) when the latency spike happens? would help confirm cache churn vs algo bug
eli: short sample: 
"Model output (mistral-1-8k quant4a, 32k): 'The system will the the the the' ... repeats at token ~21000" — repetition aligns with the latency cliff.
perf-bot: perf-bot summary: run=1758881234, model=mistral-1-8k, region=eu-west, instance=h100-x2, seq=32768, p50=420ms, p95=980ms, p99=1450ms, throughput=2.1 tok/s (baseline expected ~4.8 tok/s)
samir: can you re-run with KERNEL=force_gqa and compare? also try same run in us-west on A100 to see if it's region/image-related
eli: re-ran quick with force_gqa on eu-west: p99 back to ~760ms, throughput ~4.4 tok/s. so forcing GQA removes the spike. interesting.
jia: that suggests the auto path picked a quantized rope kernel that doesn't maintain phase the same way as our GQA kernels. we have a known smaller-block kernel for eu-west images (image build v2025.03) that may be older. infra-bot, can you check which kernel package is built into eu-west h100 images for the inference node pool used?
infra-bot: infra-bot: eu-west-inference-pool uses image id redwood-infer-h100:v2025.03. Kernel package: lr-kernels-202501, rope-quant-block=64, gqa-block=128 fallback present
marta: compare that to us-west? maybe us-west picked 128-block rope so phase matches gqa more closely
infra-bot: us-west uses redwood-infer-h100:v2025.06 with rope-quant-block=128, gqa-block=128
samir: actionable: 1) pin auto-selection to prefer gqa for Mistral on quantized profiles until rope-quant-block>=128; 2) run a quick regression test suite (quality + perf) across 8k/16k/32k for both Llama and Qwen to ensure no regressions; 3) schedule kernel bump in eu-west image.
eli: agreed. i'll open a short rollout ticket for kernel bump and add a canary job that runs the ctx-sweep every image deploy. also will add a small eval (bleu/rep rate) for long-context edge cases.
jia: one more ask — when you open the ticket, add the minimal repro (command + perf-bot numbers + sample output). will help kernel folks triage.
samir: and add a note to model onboarding checklist: "verify kernel block parity across regions for quant profiles" so this doesn't bite new models
marta: also run same check for Qwen-2 and Llama-3a; Qwen sometimes uses hybrid GQA-rope mapping when model width mismatches occur
eli: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
